population: 11 healthy adults (30-57 years) reporting persistently unsatisfactory sleep
duration: Two sets of 2 consecutive nights/days, separated by >=1 week
finding_summary: In 11 adults, 3 g glycine before bed improved selected subjective sleep-quality scores and shortened polysomnographic sleep-onset and slow-wave-sleep latencies versus placebo.
limitations: Very small, short crossover trial; single-blinded; outcomes do not establish benefit for chronic insomnia or lifespan; intervention differs from commercial supplement doses.

study_design: Placebo-controlled randomized trial in older adults; young adult non-placebo comparison cohort
studied_dose: Glycine 100 mg/kg/day plus NAC 100 mg/kg/day (GlyNAC); older-adult placebo alanine 200 mg/kg/day
population: 24 older adults randomized (12 GlyNAC; 12 alanine placebo); 12 young adults received GlyNAC for 2 weeks
duration: 16 weeks in older adults; 2 weeks in young adults
finding_summary: Authors reported changes in glutathione, oxidative stress, functional tests and multiple physiological biomarkers in older adults receiving combined GlyNAC versus alanine placebo.
limitations: Small older-adult intervention groups (12 each); many endpoints and multiplicity risk; young adults were not a matched placebo group; GlyNAC combination results cannot be attributed to glycine alone; no clinical lifespan endpoint.

studied_dose: Approx. 1,786 mg/day magnesium bisglycinate providing 250 mg/day elemental magnesium and ~1,523 mg glycine-equivalent chelate component; 2 capsules/day
finding_summary: At 4 weeks the Insomnia Severity Index decreased by 3.9 points in the magnesium-bisglycinate arm versus 2.3 with placebo (p=0.049); standardized effect was small (Cohen d about 0.2).
limitations: Self-reported insomnia severity; small effect with borderline statistical significance; study did not isolate effects of magnesium from the glycine constituent; no evidence for broad sleep outcomes, treatment of chronic insomnia or longevity.

study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 randomized controlled trials
finding_summary: Small pooled positive signal for memory (SMD approximately 0.31); no significant pooled benefit for global cognition or executive function; evidence certainty and effect vary by domain.
limitations: Heterogeneous study populations, doses and endpoints; no dementia-prevention or longevity outcomes. Publisher corrigendum (2025; PMID 40034739; DOI 10.3389/fnut.2025.1570800) corrected the wording for attention and processing-speed scores without changing conclusions.

finding_summary: Review concluded cognitive benefits were equivocal despite evidence for increased brain creatine.
limitations: Different evidence synthesis than CRE-2024-META; report both; not necessarily contradictory datasets.

finding_summary: Clinic and ambulatory blood pressure decreased relative to placebo.
limitations: Population selected for prehypertension; not general wellness or lifespan evidence.

study_design: Randomized double-blind controlled feeding trial in pregnant women; offspring follow-up
intervention: Controlled total maternal dietary choline intake during third trimester (not an isolated adult nootropic intervention)
population: 26 women in third trimester (13 per group); 24 children completed follow-up
duration: Maternal intervention from third trimester until delivery; child assessments at 4, 7, 10 and 13 months
finding_summary: Offspring of women consuming 930 mg/day total maternal choline had faster average information-processing reaction times than offspring from the 480 mg/day group.
limitations: Small pregnancy-specific study; measures infant information processing, not adult memory; cannot be generalized to healthy adults or to choline bitartrate supplementation at unrelated doses.

intervention: L-5-MTHF vs folic acid vs placebo
finding_summary: L-5-MTHF lowered plasma homocysteine versus placebo.
limitations: Biomarker endpoint, not reduction in cardiovascular events or lifespan.

study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs
intervention: B12 alone or B vitamin combinations
population: 6276 people in 16 RCTs without overt B12 deficiency
finding_summary: No overall evidence of benefit for cognitive outcomes or depression in the populations reviewed.
limitations: Does not question medical need for treatment of actual B12 deficiency.

finding_summary: No statistically significant reduction in either primary outcome.
limitations: Not a test of correcting deficiency; other outcomes beyond scope.

finding_summary: Smaller age-related decline in some bone-density measures versus placebo.
limitations: Does not establish fracture reduction or results for men and younger people.

finding_summary: 3 g and 6 g single doses lowered homocysteine; 1 g did not.
limitations: Biomarker and acute response; not cardiovascular event or lifespan evidence.

studied_dose: 500 mg nicotinamide riboside chloride twice daily (1,000 mg/day)
population: 24 healthy adults aged 55-79 years completing the 2 x 6-week crossover
duration: Two 6-week crossover periods: NR and placebo
finding_summary: NR supplementation increased NAD-related metabolites in circulating blood mononuclear cells and was well tolerated during the trial; physiological findings were exploratory.
limitations: Small short crossover study; increased blood-cell NAD+ markers do not establish benefits in other tissues, clinical health improvement, perceived energy or human longevity.

intervention: CoQ10 added to standard heart-failure treatment
outcome_domain: Heart-failure clinical events over 2 years; short-term functional and biomarker measures
finding_summary: At 16 weeks, short-term functional and biomarker outcomes were not significantly different; at 2 years, the composite major-adverse-cardiovascular-event endpoint occurred in 15% with CoQ10 vs 26% with placebo (HR 0.50; 95% CI 0.32-0.80).
limitations: 420 patients with moderate-to-severe chronic heart failure received CoQ10 as adjunctive treatment; disease-specific result does not demonstrate benefits for healthy adults or general longevity. Commercial support and trial limitations require consideration.

finding_summary: In a small 12-week RCT, authors reported differences on selected Cognitrax cognitive-domain scores versus placebo; the associated correction notice addressed minor errors in Table 4.
limitations: 64 randomized and 58 completed; multiple measured outcomes and multiplicity risk; product-specific disodium form; correction notice PMID 35917215 (DOI 10.1080/27697061.2022.2099711) updated Table 4, so numerical results must be checked against the corrected table. No evidence of dementia prevention or longer lifespan.

population: 100 older adults with subjective cognitive decline
finding_summary: No significant difference versus placebo for primary memory outcome or secondary outcomes.
limitations: Exploratory subgroup findings do not overturn negative primary outcome.

finding_summary: Meta-analysis reported modest reductions in select BP outcomes and subgroups.
limitations: Heterogeneity; not proven clinical event reduction or lifespan extension.

finding_summary: No significant improvement in measured fasting cardiometabolic risk markers versus placebo.
limitations: Short duration; findings population- and outcome-specific.

outcome_domain: Daytime fatigue, sleepiness and psychomotor vigilance
finding_summary: Reduced subjective fatigue on day 1 and improved psychomotor-vigilance performance; effects were not uniform across all measures or days.
limitations: Very small sample; single-blind; acute sleep-restriction model; company-affiliated investigators; no clinical or longevity endpoint.

study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials
intervention: Oral magnesium supplements using heterogeneous salts
finding_summary: Pooled sleep-onset latency was 17.36 minutes shorter; the estimated 16.06-minute increase in sleep duration was not statistically significant.
limitations: Only 3 small trials; moderate-to-high risk of bias; low to very low certainty; heterogeneous salts and doses; does not establish a bisglycinate-specific effect.

study_design: Preregistered randomized double-blind placebo-controlled crossover trial
population: 123 randomized healthy adults including vegetarians and omnivores
finding_summary: Neither primary cognitive endpoint reached conventional statistical significance; estimated effects were small for Raven matrices and backward digit span, and exploratory tasks were negative.
limitations: Dropout and adherence reduced analyzable observations; possible carryover; effects were much smaller than earlier estimates; adverse effects were reported more often with creatine.

intervention: Single-dose creatine monohydrate during sleep deprivation
population: 15 healthy adults undergoing approximately 21 hours of sleep deprivation
duration: Acute; outcomes assessed for up to 9 hours
outcome_domain: Cognition, fatigue and cerebral energy metabolites
finding_summary: Creatine attenuated deterioration on several cognitive tasks, reduced fatigue and changed cerebral phosphate and creatine-related magnetic-resonance spectroscopy measures.
limitations: Very small study; unusually high acute dose; sleep-deprivation model; multiple outcomes and time points; findings do not establish benefits from routine lower-dose use.

population: 103 participants across 7 studies with varied health status
finding_summary: Pooled estimates corresponded to approximately 3 mmHg reductions in both systolic and diastolic blood pressure.
limitations: Very small aggregate sample; heterogeneous populations, doses and durations; surrogate risk-factor endpoint; no cardiovascular-event or longevity evidence.

study_design: Follow-up of randomized controlled maternal feeding trial
intervention: Maternal dietary choline during the third trimester
population: Children from a small randomized maternal controlled-feeding cohort
duration: Third-trimester intervention; child assessed at age 7 years
finding_summary: Children whose mothers received the higher choline intake showed better sustained-attention performance on the study task.
limitations: Small follow-up cohort from the same parent trial as CHO-2018-INFANT; prenatal exposure only; total dietary choline rather than evidence for adult choline, citicoline or alpha-GPC supplementation.

study_design: Two randomized double-blind parallel-sequential adjunctive trials
intervention: L-methylfolate added to stable SSRI therapy
studied_dose: Trial 1: 7.5 mg/day escalating to 15 mg/day; Trial 2: 15 mg/day
population: 148 and 75 adults with SSRI-resistant major depressive disorder
finding_summary: The lower-dose first trial was negative; the second trial reported greater response with 15 mg/day adjunctive L-methylfolate than placebo.
limitations: Disease-specific adjunctive treatment at pharmacological milligram doses; small positive trial; does not support mood or longevity claims in healthy or folate-replete adults.

population: 201 adults aged at least 75 years with moderate biochemical B12 deficiency but no anemia or neurologic symptoms; 191 provided outcome data
finding_summary: B12 corrected biochemical status and lowered homocysteine but did not improve the primary nerve-conduction endpoint, other neurologic measures or cognition.
limitations: Does not apply to severe or symptomatic B12 deficiency, in which replacement remains clinically necessary; participants were comparatively healthy.

study_design: Large randomized placebo-controlled trial ancillary analysis
population: 25871 generally healthy US adults not selected for vitamin D deficiency, osteoporosis or low bone mass
finding_summary: Vitamin D3 did not significantly reduce total, nonvertebral or hip fractures compared with placebo.
limitations: Companion publication from the same VITAL parent trial as D3-2019-VITAL and therefore not an independent cohort; does not test targeted treatment of deficiency.

outcome_domain: Arterial stiffness and vitamin K status
finding_summary: MK-7 improved vitamin K status and produced modest improvements in arterial-stiffness measurements, particularly among women with higher baseline stiffness.
limitations: Surrogate vascular endpoints; subgroup sensitivity; women aged 55-65 only; no cardiovascular-event or lifespan endpoint.

outcome_domain: Body composition, energy expenditure and homocysteine
finding_summary: Betaine lowered plasma homocysteine but did not improve body weight, fat mass or resting energy expenditure beyond the hypoenergetic diet.
limitations: Small sample; selected population; biomarker benefit did not translate into the prespecified body-composition outcomes; high gram-scale dose.

population: 40 sedentary men aged 40-70 years with obesity and insulin resistance
finding_summary: NR was generally tolerated but did not improve insulin sensitivity, glucose metabolism, resting energy expenditure, lipid oxidation or body composition.
limitations: Small male-only study; obese insulin-resistant population; 12-week duration; does not address lifespan despite testing a high dose.

outcome_domain: NAD metabolites, insulin sensitivity and mitochondrial function
finding_summary: NR increased skeletal-muscle NAD-related metabolites and altered acetylcarnitine metabolism but did not improve insulin sensitivity, mitochondrial function, blood pressure, inflammation or most other metabolic outcomes.
limitations: Very small crossover study; short duration; biomarker changes should not be interpreted as demonstrated healthspan or lifespan benefit.

study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials
intervention: Coenzyme Q10 versus placebo in statin-associated muscle symptoms
outcome_domain: Statin-associated muscle pain and treatment adherence
finding_summary: CoQ10 did not significantly improve myalgia scores or the proportion of patients continuing statin therapy.
limitations: Small heterogeneous trials; inconsistent case definitions and doses; only 2 included studies reported benefit; does not negate disease-specific heart-failure evidence.

finding_summary: The study reported improvements in selected cognitive domains at 8 or 12 weeks, with different patterns in younger and older subgroups.
limitations: Small short product-specific study; subgroup analyses and multiple cognitive endpoints increase false-positive risk; no dementia, disability or longevity outcome; full funding and bias assessment remains outstanding.

study_design: Randomized placebo-controlled pharmacokinetic and metabolomic study
studied_dose: 15 mg/day regimen reported by the publication; exact schedule requires full-text confirmation
finding_summary: Supplementation increased plasma spermine but did not increase plasma or salivary spermidine, suggesting substantial presystemic conversion.
limitations: Pharmacokinetic biomarker study rather than an efficacy trial; small and short; exact schedule, sample size and funding require full-text verification.

study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials
population: 587 participants across 7 trials and 9 treatment arms
finding_summary: Pooled estimates suggested reductions of 3.04 mmHg systolic and 2.63 mmHg diastolic blood pressure; apparent effects were concentrated in trials using at least 500 mg/day.
limitations: Overlaps underlying trials with QUE-2022-META; heterogeneous populations and protocols; dose subgroup comparison was indirect; no clinical-event evidence.

population: 40 adults aged 50-80 years with mild cognitive impairment; 18 resveratrol and 22 placebo completers
outcome_domain: Memory, glucose control and hippocampal imaging
finding_summary: Resveratrol changed selected imaging measures; HbA1c and hippocampal-volume effects were borderline, and no significant between-group improvement in memory was found.
limitations: Small clinical population; multiple imaging and metabolic endpoints; borderline findings; olive-oil placebo; not generalizable to healthy adults or lifespan.

study_design: Narrative review of preclinical and human evidence
population: Preclinical studies and limited historical human studies
outcome_domain: Aging, metabolism and human evidence gaps
finding_summary: The review found encouraging animal and mechanistic evidence but no contemporary human trials demonstrating treatment of aging or age-related disease.
limitations: Narrative review rather than a systematic review; animal findings cannot establish human efficacy; not a trial of a commercial Ca-AKG regimen.

population: Planned 120 healthy adults aged 40-60 years with DNA methylation age above chronological age
outcome_domain: DNA methylation age and exploratory physiological outcomes
finding_summary: Protocol specifies DNA methylation age as the primary endpoint; it contains no efficacy result and cannot support a benefit claim.
limitations: Protocol only; surrogate primary endpoint of uncertain clinical meaning; selected biologically older subgroup; no morbidity, mortality or lifespan endpoint.
